mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a UNRATE decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses below 0.15%, it indicates monetary easing, which stimulates economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 55% of the 60-day windows after FEDFUNDS falls below 0.15%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) increase, it signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the 20-day windows following simultaneous increases in GDPC1 and HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals increased supply and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 60% of the 60-day windows following an INDPRO increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 45% of the 5-day windows following an RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 100,000 jobs, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 60% of the 20-day windows following a PAYEMS increase above 100,000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.15% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8%, it signals a specific policy stance, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following the specified conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in housing starts (HOUST) during a late-cycle expansion signals reduced demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative returns in at least 50% of the 20-day windows following a HOUST slowdown, the hypothesis is rejected.
